RACHEL WILDE / WORKING PROTOTYPE

A good idea needs
a way forward.

Make the Case helps people use their knowledge of work to develop an improvement, identify the evidence and people it needs, and keep a record of their contribution. It is one practical part of a larger question: how does an organization turn employee insight and leadership priorities into supported, governed work with measurable outcomes?

The decisions behind the design

ChoiceWhy it matters
Start from the workA person's title or technical skills do not determine the value of their insight. Discovery, evidence, coordination, review, and adoption are contributions too.
Keep every ideaSelecting one focus should preserve alternatives, dependencies, and reasons to revisit an opportunity.
Make assumptions visibleChecking, correction, support, coverage, and uptake can change an attractive estimate. A forecast remains a hypothesis.
Connect people and authorityA positive estimate still needs appropriate ownership, permissions, learning, support, and a bounded next commitment.
Retain the reasoningExported context, ideas, decisions, and contribution records let a person resume or collaborate without rebuilding a case from memory.

Try the consequential assumption

The fictional Northstar example releases a forecast 4.4 hours/month. Increase checking and correction to 20 minutes per task: it adds 5.2 net hours/month of work. The recommendation changes to revisiting the approach. A different benefit might still justify an investigation, but the time-saving claim no longer holds.

The example retains a permission-review condition in either scenario. A calculated benefit cannot grant authority.

Where AI belongs

The reusable method guides an AI assistant to interview, challenge assumptions, compare alternatives, and develop a case. The workspace can prepare that briefing with your current context. The browser itself makes no model calls; its forecasts and next-step checks use explicit calculations and rules.

Your records are kept in this browser. They are not automatically uploaded, sent to an employer, or shared with an AI provider. An export or a copied briefing is under your control. Browser storage can be cleared, so download a workspace file to keep your work. Use information your organization permits you to process and share.

What Rachel contributed

Rachel defined the problem through research into AI change management, challenged a narrow proposal-generator framing, and established an inclusive process connecting ideas, evidence, collaborators, governance, and recognition. AI assisted research, synthesis, implementation, and verification. The project makes those design choices inspectable rather than claiming unmeasured business or career outcomes.

Evidence and limits

Northstar and all of its evidence are fictional. The prototype includes automated calculation, validation, and continuity checks. It has not been field-validated, and no claim is made that it protects jobs, secures promotions, proves legal compliance, or improves financial outcomes. Assistant portability is a design goal; comparative provider testing is not complete.

A conversation about the bigger issue

Where does an improvement idea stall in your organization: scoping it, proving the value, finding an owner, getting approval, or making the change stick?

Automation Thursday is the public experiment. Reader use, practical questions, and conversations with leaders can help determine which parts of the wider operating framework deserve attention next.
